key_insight: GRADE is the first benchmark that measures discipline-informed knowledge and reasoning in image editing, revealing that current multimodal models struggle with domain-specific, constraint-driven edits beyond commonsense scenarios.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of evaluation for structured, domain-specific reasoning in image editing by providing a curated benchmark that tests models on edits requiring academic-discipline knowledge and constraints.
method: Curate 520 high-quality editing examples across 10 academic domains (e.g., chemistry, medicine, engineering) that require discipline-specific constraints and rationale.
Define task templates and evaluation metrics focused on correctness of edits, preservation of domain constraints, and quality of explanations/rationales.
Benchmark multiple unified multimodal models to quantify failure modes and provide baselines for discipline-informed editing performance.
impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to diagnose and improve multimodal models' ability to perform safe, accurate, and constraint-aware edits in scientific and technical contexts, guiding development of more reliable domain-aware generative systems.

paper_title: GRADE: Benchmarking Discipline-Informed Reasoning in Image Editing
paper_authors: Mingxin Liu, Ziqian Fan, Zhaokai Wang, Leyao Gu, Zirun Zhu
